author: G.R.Gray, 1845
summary: 열대 대양에 사는 큰 바닷새로, 가끔 우리나라 바다에도 나타난다. 낮에는 하늘을 날다가 빠르게 내리꽂혀 파도 사이로 튀어 오르는 물고기를 잡고, 다른 바닷새를 괴롭혀 토해 낸 먹이를 가로채기도 한다. 때로는 배를 따라다니며, 번식기가 아니면 내륙에서는 보기 어렵다. 섬의 나무에 나뭇가지로 엉성한 접시 모양 둥지를 짓고, 주로 물고기를 먹는다.

points.en: white patches on the sides of the belly (male)
brown bar on the wing coverts (female)

sexes.male: 배 양쪽의 흰 얼룩을 빼면 대부분 검은색이나 흑갈색이고, 턱 밑에 커다란 붉은 공기주머니가 있다.
sexes.female: 뒷목에 밤색 가로띠, 날개덮깃에 갈색 띠가 있고 가슴은 유백색이다.

young: 어린새는 머리가 연한 주황빛 갈색이고, 가슴의 검은 띠 아래 배에 아래쪽으로 뾰족한 삼각형 흰 무늬가 있으며 흰색이 겨드랑이까지 뻗는다. 어른 깃을 갖추기까지 여러 해가 걸린다.

art.subject: Lesser Frigatebird (Fregata ariel), adult male in flight over the sea: entire plumage black with a faint green-purple gloss on the head and back, except a white patch on each side of the belly that extends as a narrow white spur into the armpit at the base of the underwing; the red throat pouch deflated, showing only as a small patch of red bare skin on the throat; long, strongly hooked bill dark grey; dark eye; tiny legs and feet tucked into the body.
art.pose: soaring high over the sea on long wings
art.scene: open sea off the Korean coast with breaking waves; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, in flight seen from below: all-black body and wings, white patch on each side of the belly continuing as a white spur into the underwing armpit, small red throat patch, long hooked grey bill, deeply forked tail

adult female, in flight banking, seen from the side and slightly below: black head and throat, chestnut-brown collar on the hindneck, white breast extending as white spurs into the underwing armpits, pale brown bar across the upperwing coverts on the raised wing
art.build: Large, slim seabird with a far greater wingspan than a Black-tailed Gull, almost always seen soaring. Wings very long, narrow and sharply pointed, strongly bent at the wrist into an M shape. Tail long and deeply forked, often held closed as a single spike. Bill long and slender with a strongly hooked tip, longer than the head. Legs tiny, feet small; never swims or rests on the water. Glides on motionless wings for long periods and swoops to snatch prey from the surface.
avoid: Do not paint the red throat pouch inflated like a balloon on a flying bird; it is inflated only in display at the breeding colony.
Do not paint the male's white across the breast or the centre of the belly; it is limited to the flank patches and spurs.
Do not paint straight gull-like or cormorant-like wings, a short square tail or a straight bill.
Do not show the bird swimming or resting on the water.
